//: Runnable programs extracted from tutorial markdown. 'blocks' selects which fenced typescript blocks to concatenate — tutorials often split one program across blocks, while other blocks are alternatives that redeclare the same names and cannot be combined. Run them all with: node test-all.mjs

programs.name: moonwalk
programs.note: standalone add-on, not extracted from markdown
programs.description: Backslide. PU travels backward while its legs make forward stepping motions. The planted leg drives back slowly — that is what actually moves it — while the unweighted leg snaps forward like a step. Button A starts it 0.2s in. Best seen from the side.

programs.name: dance-builtin
programs.description: The extension's built-in beat-reactive dance. It listens to the microphone, changes pose every few beats and wiggles the head with volume. Driven here by a synthetic 120 BPM beat.

programs.name: dance-beatsync
programs.note: Parts 3+4 — block 2 needs block 1's setPose/gaits. Static without --sound.
programs.description: A hand-written beat detector: when loudness crosses a threshold it steps to a new pose from a six-gait table, easing smoothly between them. In a quiet room this program never moves.

programs.name: dance-qlearn
programs.note: Part 6 — self-contained; redeclares names from blocks 1-2, cannot combine
programs.description: A dance that learns. A Q-table picks the next pose transition, rewarded by loud 'crowd noise' and penalised by falls, so it gradually settles on a favourite routine.

programs.name: motor-pose
programs.note: pose helpers + easing; block 8 transitions at top level, so motion lands before bootMs
programs.description: Pose interpolation demo. Eases between a standing pose and a crouch, first with linear blending and then with smooth-step easing, so you can compare how the two feel.

programs.name: motor-bow
programs.note: doBow() on button A; needs blocks 0-5 for transitionPose
programs.description: PU takes a bow when button A is pressed: the head pitches down to 140 degrees and back up, eased in and out so the motion looks deliberate rather than abrupt.

programs.name: motor-remote
programs.description: Remote-control demo. Poses are driven through the same radio command handlers the gamepad uses, rather than by calling the servos directly.

programs.name: motor-step-a
programs.description: Convergence demo. Every joint is pushed toward a target a small step at a time, looping until all the position errors reach zero.

programs.name: motor-step-b
programs.description: The same convergence loop as motor-step-a, but with a different step size per joint, so the legs arrive more slowly than the head and arms.

programs.name: motor-i2c-read
programs.note: raw bus probe — selects a register and reads it back; moves nothing
programs.description: Raw bus probe: selects a servo register over I2C and reads the value back. The robot does not move — this one is about talking to the board, not driving it.

programs.name: motor-i2c-write
programs.note: raw bus ACK probe; moves nothing
programs.description: Raw bus probe that writes a single byte to check the servo board acknowledges. No motion.

programs.name: yoga-routine
programs.note: Stand/Jump/Yoga sequence. Adapted from the beginner `robotPu` namespace to `robotPuPro`. NEEDS --i2c-us: its while-loops drive servos with no basic.pause(), so at zero bus cost the whole motion collapses into one instant.
programs.description: Repeats a Stand, Jump, Yoga, Yoga2, Yoga3 loop. Jump and Yoga both split the ankles hard enough to lift one foot clear of the ground; Yoga2 and Yoga3 sweep the right leg between its extremes while the head turns to follow.

programs.name: yoga-sequence
programs.note: Stand/Jump/Yoga/Yoga2/Yoga3 run ONCE. Needs --i2c-us (while-loops have no basic.pause). --skip-boot is a no-op here: the first servo() call is inside forever(), so ensureRobot()'s ~3.5s calibrate+start lands in the run window, not before it.
programs.description: One pass through Stand, Jump, Yoga, Yoga2 and Yoga3. Jump splits the ankles 55 degrees and Yoga 70 degrees, each lifting a foot off the ground, then Yoga2 and Yoga3 sweep the right leg from 20 to 170 degrees. Ends standing.

programs.name: kungfu
programs.note: Four-gait kungfu routine. Uses TWO forever loops (fast moveServos action engine + slow 2s gait selector) - the pattern that exposed the forever-loop starvation bug. Blocks 0/1 are data literals, 3 is a subset of 2, 4 is a line lifted from inside 2's loop.
programs.description: Cycles four kungfu poses, holding each for two seconds: stand, raise a hand on tiptoe, spread both arms, then a wide leg split. A fast action engine eases every joint toward whichever pose is currently selected.

programs.name: kungfu-legs
programs.description: Kungfu for a robot with no arm servos. Four poses, two seconds each: ready stance, tiptoe with a front kick, forward lunge, then a wide leg split. Every shape is made with the legs and head; the arm servos stay at 90 throughout.
programs.note: Leg-only rewrite of tutorials/kungfu.md. The original puts three of its four gaits in the shoulders/arms (servos 6-9), which are optional hardware.
